347	func (m searchModel) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) { //nolint:cyclop // bubbletea interface
348		switch msg := msg.(type) {
349		case searchResultsMsg:
350			m.loading = false
351			m.fetchingMore = false
352			if msg.err != nil {
353				m.searchErr = RenderUserFacingError(msg.err).Error()
354				m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
355				return m, nil
356			}
357			m.searchErr = ""
358			m.results = msg.results
359			m.total = msg.total
360			m.counts = msg.counts
361			m.countsLowerBound = msg.countsLowerBound
362			m.warning = strings.Join(msg.warnings, "; ")
363			m.apiPage = 1
364			m.cursor = 0
365			m.page = 0
366			m.browseVP.GotoTop()
367			m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
368			return m, nil
369	
370		case searchMoreResultsMsg:
371			m.fetchingMore = false
372			if msg.err != nil {
373				m.searchErr = RenderUserFacingError(msg.err).Error()
374				m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
375				return m, nil
376			}
377			if len(msg.warnings) > 0 {
378				m.warning = strings.Join(msg.warnings, "; ")

381			if len(msg.results) > 0 {

385				// pull the display page back into range (paging forward advanced
386				// it optimistically before the fetch came back empty).
387				m.total = len(m.results)
388				if last := m.totalPages() - 1; m.page > last {
389					m.page = last
390					m.cursor = 0
391				}
392			}
393			m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
394			return m, nil
395	
396		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
397			m.width = msg.Width
398			m.height = msg.Height
399			m.input.SetWidth(max(msg.Width-6, 30))
400			m.browseVP.SetWidth(msg.Width)
401			m.browseVP.SetHeight(max(msg.Height-1, 1)) // reserve 1 line for footer
402			if m.mode == modeDetail {
403				m.detailVP.SetWidth(msg.Width)
404				m.detailVP.SetHeight(max(msg.Height-2, 1))
405			}
406			m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
407			return m, nil
408	
409		case codeSearchResultsMsg:
410			if msg.gen != m.codeSearchGen {
411				return m, nil // stale result from a superseded search
412			}
413			m.codeLoading = false
414			if msg.err != nil {
415				m.codeSearchErr = RenderUserFacingError(msg.err).Error()
416			} else if msg.resp != nil {
417				m.codeResults = msg.resp.Results
418				m.codeStats = msg.resp.Stats
419				m.codeSearchErr = ""
420				m.codeWarning = codeSearchWarning(msg.resp)
421			}
422			if m.filterType == typeFilterCode {
423				m.cursor = 0
424				m.page = 0
425				m.browseVP.GotoTop()
426			}
427			m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
428			return m, nil
429	
430		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
431			switch m.mode {
432			case modeSearch:
433				return m.updateSearchMode(msg)
434			case modeDetail:
435				return m.updateDetailMode(msg)
436			case modeBrowse:
437				return m.updateBrowseMode(msg)
438			}
439		}
440		return m, nil

443	func (m searchModel) updateSearchMode(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
444		switch {
445		case key.Matches(msg, keys.Back):
446			m.mode = modeBrowse
447			m.input.Blur()
448			m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
449			return m, nil
450		case key.Matches(msg, keys.Confirm):
451			raw := strings.TrimSpace(m.input.Value())
452			if raw == "" {
453				return m, nil
454			}
455			// Checkpoint search: ParseSearchInput extracts author:/date:/branch:/repo:.
456			// ValidateRepoFilters only checks each repo value's shape; both semantic
457			// and code search accept multiple repos and fan out across cells.
458			parsed := search.ParseSearchInput(raw)
459			checkpointRepoErr := search.ValidateRepoFilters(parsed.Repos)
460	
461			m.searchErr = ""
462	
463			var cmds []tea.Cmd
464			willFireCodeSearch := false
465	
466			// Code search uses extractInlineRepoFilters (not ParseSearchInput)
467			// so author:/date:/branch: tokens are preserved as literal search
468			// text, matching the --code CLI path.
469			codeQuery, inlineRepos := extractInlineRepoFilters(raw)
470			if codeQuery != "" {
471				willFireCodeSearch = true
472				opts := m.codeSearchOpts
473				opts.query = codeQuery
474				// Always reset to the model's default repo scope, then apply
475				// inline overrides. This prevents a stale repo list from a
476				// previous query leaking into the next one.
477				opts.repoFilters = m.codeSearchOpts.repoFilters
478				if len(inlineRepos) > 0 {
479					if hasAllReposFilter(inlineRepos) {
480						opts.repoFilters = nil
481					} else {
482						opts.repoFilters = filterRepoWildcards(inlineRepos)
483					}
484				}
485				m.codeSearchGen++
486				m.codeLoading = true
487				m.codeResults = nil
488				m.codeSearchErr = ""
489				m.codeWarning = ""
490				cmds = append(cmds, performCodeSearch(opts, m.codeSearchGen))
491			} else {
492				// No code query (e.g. repo-only input) — clear stale code
493				// results and bump the generation so any in-flight search
494				// from a prior query is discarded when it completes. Nothing
495				// will arrive to overwrite the warning, so clear it here too.
496				m.codeSearchGen++
497				m.codeLoading = false
498				m.codeResults = nil
499				m.codeSearchErr = ""
500				m.codeWarning = ""
501			}
502	
503			// Checkpoint search (only if repo filters are valid for the checkpoint API).
504			if checkpointRepoErr != nil {
505				m.searchErr = checkpointRepoErr.Error()
506				if !willFireCodeSearch {
507					// Neither search will fire — stay in search mode so the
508					// user can correct the input without pressing / again.
509					m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
510					return m, nil
511				}
512			} else {
513				m.loading = true
514				cfg := m.searchCfg
515				cfg.Query = parsed.Query
516				if cfg.Query == "" {
517					cfg.Query = search.WildcardQuery
518				}
519				cfg.Author = parsed.Author
520				cfg.Date = parsed.Date
521				cfg.Branch = parsed.Branch
522				cfg.Repos = parsed.Repos
523				m.searchCfg = cfg
524				cmds = append(cmds, m.performSearch(cfg))
525			}
526	
527			m.mode = modeBrowse
528			m.input.Blur()
529			m = m.refreshBrowseContent()
530			return m, tea.Batch(cmds...)
531		}

564		var pageLen int
565		if m.filterType == typeFilterCode {
566			pageLen = len(m.codePageResults())
567		} else {
568			pageLen = len(m.pageResults())
569		}

731	// viewBrowse composes the browse screen as a fixed master-detail layout:
732	//
733	//	┌ header  (search title, query, tabs, RESULTS) — pinned top
734	//	│ list    (scrollable result rows in browseVP)
735	//	│ detail  (bordered card for the selected row) — pinned bottom
736	//	└ footer  (help line) — pinned very bottom
737	//
738	// Heights are budgeted from the terminal height so the detail card is always
739	// fully visible and can never be clipped, regardless of how the list scrolls.
740	func (m searchModel) viewBrowse() string {
741		footer := strings.TrimRight(m.viewHelp(), "\n")
742		header, showList := m.viewBrowseHeader()
743	
744		var body string
745		switch {
746		case !showList:
747			// Loading / error / empty states: header is the whole body; pin the
748			// footer to the bottom of the screen.
749			body = padToHeight(header, max(m.height-1, 0)) + "\n" + footer
750		default:
751			paneH := m.detailPaneHeight(lipgloss.Height(header))
752			// browseVP height is kept in sync by refreshBrowseContent; render
753			// whatever window it currently exposes.
754			list := m.browseVP.View()
755			// The reserved row beneath the list shows the page/results count (and a
756			// scroll affordance when rows are cut off).
757			gap := m.viewListStatusRow()
758			if paneH <= 0 {
759				body = header + "\n" + list + "\n" + gap + "\n" + footer
760			} else {
761				body = header + "\n" + list + "\n" + gap + "\n" + m.viewDetailPane(paneH) + "\n" + footer
762			}
763		}
764	
765		// Final safety net: on a terminal too short to fit even the pinned chrome,
766		// clamp so we never emit more rows than the screen (which would scroll the
767		// alt-screen and clip the top). Exactly-budgeted layouts are unaffected.
768		return clampToHeight(body, m.height)
769	}

771	// padToHeight pads s with blank lines so it occupies exactly n lines (or leaves
772	// it unchanged when already taller). Used to push a pinned footer to the bottom.
773	func padToHeight(s string, n int) string {
774		h := lipgloss.Height(s)
775		if h >= n {
776			return s
777		}
778		return s + strings.Repeat("\n", n-h)
779	}
780	
781	// clampToHeight returns at most the first n lines of s.
782	func clampToHeight(s string, n int) string {
783		if n <= 0 {
784			return ""
785		}
786		lines := strings.Split(s, "\n")
787		if len(lines) <= n {
788			return s
789		}
790		return strings.Join(lines[:n], "\n")
791	}

921	// refreshBrowseContent rebuilds the scrollable list viewport and re-applies the
922	// master-detail layout (list height + cursor visibility) for the current state.
923	func (m searchModel) refreshBrowseContent() searchModel {
924		// Trim the trailing newline so the viewport's line count reflects the real
925		// number of rows (a phantom blank line would keep "scroll down" lit at the
926		// bottom of the list).
927		m.browseVP.SetContent(strings.TrimRight(m.viewResultList(), "\n"))
928	
929		if m.height <= 0 || m.width == 0 {
930			return m
931		}
932		header, showList := m.viewBrowseHeader()
933		if !showList {
934			return m
935		}
936		headerLines := lipgloss.Height(header)
937		paneH := m.detailPaneHeight(headerLines)
938		// Always reserve the gap/scroll-hint row and the footer row.
939		listH := max(m.height-headerLines-paneH-detailGap-1, 1)
940		m.browseVP.SetHeight(listH)
941		return m.ensureCursorVisible()
942	}

944	// detailPaneHeight returns the number of terminal rows reserved for the pinned
945	// detail pane, or 0 when there is no selection or the screen is too short to
946	// pin one (in which case the list takes the full area and detail is reachable
947	// via the full-screen view). headerLines is the height of the pinned top chrome.
948	func (m searchModel) detailPaneHeight(headerLines int) int {
949		hasSelection := m.selectedResult() != nil
950		if m.filterType == typeFilterCode {
951			codeResults := m.codePageResults()
952			hasSelection = m.cursor >= 0 && m.cursor < len(codeResults)
953		}
954		if m.height <= 0 || !hasSelection {
955			return 0
956		}
957		avail := m.height - 1 - headerLines - detailGap // footer + gap rows
958		if avail < minListHeight+minDetailPaneHeight {
959			return 0
960		}
961		h := m.height * 2 / 5 // ~40% of the screen
962		h = min(max(h, minDetailPaneHeight), maxDetailPaneHeight)
963		if h > avail-minListHeight {
964			h = avail - minListHeight
965		}
966		return h
967	}

969	// ensureCursorVisible scrolls the list viewport so the selected row stays
970	// within the visible window as the cursor moves.
971	func (m searchModel) ensureCursorVisible() searchModel {
972		listH := m.browseVP.Height()
973		if listH <= 0 {
974			return m
975		}
976		top := m.cursor * linesPerResult // first line of the selected item
977		bottom := top + 1                // each item occupies 2 lines
978		yo := m.browseVP.YOffset()
979		switch {
980		case top < yo:
981			yo = top
982		case bottom > yo+listH-1:
983			yo = bottom - listH + 1
984		}
985		m.browseVP.SetYOffset(max(yo, 0))
986		return m
987	}

989	// viewListStatusRow renders the single reserved row directly beneath the result
990	// list: a "more results" scroll affordance on the left (only when rows are
991	// scrolled out of view) and the page / total-results indicator on the right.
992	// It is exactly one line wide (never wraps) so the layout budget holds.
993	func (m searchModel) viewListStatusRow() string {
994		contentWidth := max(m.width-2, 0)
995	
996		// Left: scroll affordance when the list viewport can't show every row.
997		left := ""
998		if listH := m.browseVP.Height(); listH > 0 {
999			if total := m.browseVP.TotalLineCount(); total > listH {
1000				yo := m.browseVP.YOffset()
1001				switch {
1002				case yo > 0 && yo+listH < total:
1003					left = "↑↓ more results"
1004				case yo+listH < total:
1005					left = "↓ more results"
1006				default:
1007					left = "↑ more results"
1008				}
1009			}
1010		}
1011	
1012		// Right: page X/Y · N results (drops the page clause for a single page).
1013		var n int
1014		if m.filterType == typeFilterCode {
1015			n = len(m.codeResults)
1016		} else {
1017			n = len(m.filteredResults())
1018		}
1019		right := fmt.Sprintf("%d results", n)
1020		if pages := m.totalPages(); pages > 1 {
1021			right = fmt.Sprintf("page %d/%d · %d results", m.page+1, pages, n)
1022		}
1023		warning := m.warning
1024		if m.filterType == typeFilterCode {
1025			warning = m.codeWarning
1026		}
1027		if warning != "" {
1028			right = "⚠ " + warning + " · " + right
1029		}
1030		if lipgloss.Width(right) > contentWidth {
1031			right = stringutil.TruncateRunes(right, contentWidth, "…")
1032		}
1033	
1034		// Drop the scroll hint if both can't fit on one row.
1035		if lipgloss.Width(left)+1+lipgloss.Width(right) > contentWidth {
1036			left = ""
1037		}
1038		gap := max(contentWidth-lipgloss.Width(left)-lipgloss.Width(right), 1)
1039	
1040		return " " + m.styles.render(m.styles.dim, left) +
1041			strings.Repeat(" ", gap) + m.styles.render(m.styles.dim, right)
1042	}

1482	// viewDetailPane renders the pinned detail card for the selected result,
1483	// sized to exactly paneH terminal rows. Content taller than the pane is
1484	// truncated with a "▼ enter for more" hint (the full content is always
1485	// available via the full-screen detail view). Shorter content is padded so
1486	// the pane occupies its full allotment and the footer stays pinned.
1487	func (m searchModel) viewDetailPane(paneH int) string {
1488		if paneH <= 0 {
1489			return strings.TrimSuffix(padToHeight("", paneH), "\n")
1490		}
1491	
1492		// Code tab uses codeResults; other tabs use selectedResult().
1493		var r *search.Result
1494		if m.filterType == typeFilterCode {
1495			codeResults := m.codePageResults()
1496			if m.cursor < 0 || m.cursor >= len(codeResults) {
1497				return strings.TrimSuffix(padToHeight("", paneH), "\n")
1498			}
1499		} else {
1500			r = m.selectedResult()
1501			if r == nil {
1502				return strings.TrimSuffix(padToHeight("", paneH), "\n")
1503			}
1504		}
1505	
1506		var contentWidth, borderWidth, chrome int
1507		if m.styles.colorEnabled {
1508			// lipgloss v2 .Width(W) is the outer width: it absorbs horizontal padding
1509			// (2+2) and the rounded border (1+1), so the inner text area is W-6.
1510			// .Height(H) yields H + vertical-padding(0) + border(2) rendered rows, so
1511			// vertical chrome is 2. Wrapping content to W-6 keeps the card at its
1512			// budgeted height.
1513			borderWidth = max(m.width-3, 0)
1514			contentWidth = max(borderWidth-6, 0)
1515			chrome = 2
1516		} else {
1517			// NO_COLOR: a leading dim rule stands in for the top border.
1518			contentWidth = max(m.width-1, 0)
1519			chrome = 1
1520		}
1521	
1522		contentLines := max(paneH-chrome, 1)
1523		var detailContent string
1524		if m.filterType == typeFilterCode {
1525			codeResults := m.codePageResults()
1526			if m.cursor >= 0 && m.cursor < len(codeResults) {
1527				detailContent = m.renderCodeDetail(codeResults[m.cursor], contentWidth, false)
1528			}
1529		} else {
1530			detailContent = m.renderDetailContent(*r, contentWidth, false)
1531		}
1532		lines := strings.Split(detailContent, "\n")
1533		if len(lines) > contentLines {
1534			lines = lines[:contentLines]
1535			hint := m.styles.render(m.styles.dim, "▼ enter for more")
1536			lines[contentLines-1] = strings.Repeat(" ", max(contentWidth-lipgloss.Width(hint), 0)) + hint
1537		}
1538		// Hard-cap each line to the inner width (ANSI-aware) so no line wraps inside
1539		// the bordered box and inflates the card past its budgeted height. This keeps
1540		// the pane exactly paneH rows tall regardless of detail content.
1541		for i, ln := range lines {
1542			if lipgloss.Width(ln) > contentWidth {
1543				lines[i] = xansi.Truncate(ln, contentWidth, "…")
1544			}
1545		}
1546		body := strings.Join(lines, "\n")
1547	
1548		if m.styles.colorEnabled {
1549			card := m.styles.detailBorder.Width(borderWidth).Height(contentLines).Render(body)
1550			return strings.TrimSuffix(indentLines(card, " "), "\n")
1551		}
1552	
1553		pane := " " + m.styles.horizontalRule(contentWidth) + "\n" + strings.TrimSuffix(indentLines(body, " "), "\n")
1554		return padToHeight(pane, paneH)
1555	}

1612	// wrapText wraps text to the given width, breaking at word boundaries.
1613	// Existing newlines in the input are preserved.
1614	func wrapText(text string, width int) string {
1615		if width <= 0 {
1616			return text
1617		}
1618		var result strings.Builder
1619		for i, paragraph := range strings.Split(text, "\n") {
1620			if i > 0 {
1621				result.WriteByte('\n')
1622			}
1623			wrapParagraph(&result, paragraph, width)
1624		}
1625		return result.String()
1626	}

1628	func wrapParagraph(b *strings.Builder, text string, width int) {
1629		words := strings.Fields(text)
1630		if len(words) == 0 {
1631			return
1632		}
1633		lineLen := 0
1634		for i, w := range words {
1635			wLen := len(w)
1636			if i == 0 {
1637				b.WriteString(w)
1638				lineLen = wLen
1639				continue
1640			}
1641			if lineLen+1+wLen > width {

content.text:
Audit done — the search TUI was already on the platform palette, with one small deviation now fixed and pushed (`68953e354`).

**The pink is the platform standard.** All CLI colors come from one package, `cmd/entire/cli/palette`, which maps to base16 ANSI slots (so your terminal theme decides the exact shade — your theme renders Magenta as pink). The standard semantic set:

| Alias | Slot | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `Accent` (the "pink") | Magenta | status agent names & checkpoint bullets, experts titles/selection, dispatch title/spinner, explain IDs, recap, markdown H1, forms — and search titles/tabs/selection |
| `Accent2` | BrightMagenta | detail-card framing (search), recap team color |
| `Muted` | BrightBlack | all dim text, borders, help footers |
| `Success` / `Error` | Green / Red | additions/deletions, status states |
| `Warning` / `Info` | Yellow / Cyan | warnings, labels/links |

Search's per-type node colors (checkpoint = magenta, session = bright magenta, commit = blue, code = green) are deliberate one-off slot uses the palette doc permits.

**The one real mismatch, fixed:** links inside search snippets were Blue/Blue while the CLI's shared markdown renderer (`mdrender`, used by recap/explain) renders Cyan URLs with Blue link text. Snippets now use the same pair, and the Blue constant was renamed `searchCommitAccent` to reflect its remaining job.

If the pink surprised you because the web platform uses a different brand color: the palette comment notes the CLI accent "was orange" and was deliberately moved to Magenta — changing that would be a one-line edit in `palette.go` that restyles every command at once, but that's a product call, not a search-TUI one.
